title: Line Art — An idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: Idea to system
scenes.purpose: A monoline light bulb (the idea) draws itself, ignites a single copper spark, and its contours extend into a connected, tonally hatched network with a word-by-word caption.
visuals: Flat stationary ink-teal field #111C22 with off-white #EEF1EC round-capped contours
Tonal hatching band (single hatch 150–220px radius, crosshatch toward the rim) in #46646E
Copper #B77843 accent limited to the hub spark and three active nodes
Gray #93A7AB header labels, dotted orbit and caption rule

beats.development: Bulb contour draws from its crown down both sides, base lines and filament follow, shadow-side hatching strokes in; copper hub spark ignites at the filament apex.
Spokes draw outward from the hub by stroke length; each node ring closes when its spoke arrives; the outer ring traces its perimeter and the dotted orbit settles.
Tonal hatching sweeps left to right, outer links and nodes extend, cross links close the loops, three nodes take the copper active state; caption rule draws and the caption reveals word by word.
Full composition settled and held for reading.

findings: Draw durations scale with stroke length (spokes ~520px/s) rather than one preset.
Primary focus moves bulb → hub → network; hatching and caption are overlapping secondary actions, as in the reviewed source grammar.
Everything is complete by about 2.22s, before the 2.7s settle deadline.
justifiedHolds: 2.25–3.0s full-scene reading hold for the six-word caption and finished network.

notes: Silent preview: no audio track, music or effects.
Background is a scene-dependent ink-teal night field, not the prior #FAF8F1 swatch; source frames informed construction grammar only, and no source subject, branding or wording was copied.
STYLE.json lists no preview_recipes, so this refresh demonstrates the primary Line Art style.
